documents.title: Follow-up DM; new exertional chest tightness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: diabetes f/u. Also mentions chest tightness.

HPI: Routine visit, but on review of systems he describes about a month of chest tightness when climbing the two flights at work or walking up the hill on his usual route. Center of chest, "like a band," no radiation he has noticed. Comes on after a minute or two of the climb and goes away within a few minutes of stopping. Never at rest, never woken him at night, no syncope, palpitations or sweating with it. No change in frequency over the month. Not related to meals. He had chalked it up to being out of shape.
Diabetes otherwise steady; still walking (on flat ground mostly now), weight 87.8 kg. Feet numb, no wounds.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 20, aspirin 81, sildenafil 50 prn.
Risk: T2DM ~18 yrs, HTN, hyperlipidemia, PAD, CKD 1, father with MI at 65. Never smoker.

Exam: BP 141/79, HR 71, SpO2 98%. Comfortable at rest. No JVD. Clear breath sounds bilaterally. Regular rhythm; no murmur, rub or gallop. Chest wall nontender. No edema. Pedal pulses diminished (known).
Resting ECG today: normal, no ischemic changes.

A/P:
1. Exertional chest tightness - typical pattern for angina in a diabetic with vascular disease until proven otherwise. Stable over a month, no rest symptoms, normal resting ECG. Referred to cardiology for evaluation and stress testing. Continue aspirin and statin. Told him plainly: chest pain at rest, lasting more than 15 minutes, or with sweating, nausea or shortness of breath = call 911, do not drive himself. No sildenafil if he has any chest symptoms that day; avoid exertion that brings it on until cardiology sees him.
2. T2DM - A1c, BMP today.
3. HTN - amlodipine 5; home readings at goal per pt.
4. PAD, neuropathy - foot exam stable.

RTC after cardiology.

conditions.label: Angina pectoris
conditions.note: stable angina, medical management per cardiology 07/26/2023

reports.text: Cardiology clinic resting ECG. Sinus rhythm. Normal intervals and axis. No ST or T-wave abnormality.

Treadmill exercise ECG, Bruce protocol.
Indication: exertional chest pressure.
Baseline ECG normal. Exercise stopped for fatigue after reaching target heart rate.
ECG: ST-segment depression developing with exercise, resolving in recovery. No ST elevation. No arrhythmia. Blood pressure response appropriate.
reports.conclusion: Positive exercise ECG for ischemia: exercise-induced ST depression with typical symptoms. No arrhythmia.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation (visit 07/26/2023)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOVASCULAR ASSOCIATES - CONSULTATION
Date: 07/26/2023
Patient: Gary Kowalczyk, 62-year-old man
Referring: primary care
Reason: exertional chest discomfort

History of present illness: Four months of central chest pressure, tight in quality, brought on by climbing stairs or walking uphill and relieved by rest within minutes. No rest pain, palpitations or syncope. Background of type 2 diabetes with neuropathy, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and peripheral arterial disease, all treated.

Medications (patient-provided list): metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).
Social: does not smoke or drink alcohol.
Family history: father with myocardial infarction at 65.

Examination: BP 132/78, pulse 72/min, BMI 27. Comfortable. JVP not raised. Heart sounds normal, no murmur. Lungs clear. No peripheral edema.

Investigations today:
- Resting 12-lead ECG: normal.
- High-sensitivity troponin: within normal limits.
- Treadmill exercise test: positive for exercise-induced ST depression; no arrhythmia.

Impression: Stable angina pectoris. Symptoms are predictable, exertional and unchanged in pattern; no features of an acute coronary syndrome.

Plan:
- Medical management. Continue aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin; continue current blood pressure treatment.
- Risk factor control with primary care: blood pressure, diabetes, lipids, activity within symptom limits.
- Return to clinic in 12 months, sooner for any change in pattern, rest pain or prolonged episodes; call 911 for pain lasting over 15 minutes.

Thank you for this referral.
Cardiology

documents.title: Your cardiology visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Gary,
I have the cardiologist's letter and your stress test. The stress test showed changes on the EKG during exercise that fit with narrowing in the heart arteries causing the chest tightness. That is called stable angina. Cardiology's plan is medicines and risk factors rather than a procedure for now, and they'll see you yearly.
Their medication list still had lisinopril on it - I sent them a corrected list (amlodipine, not lisinopril).
Please book a visit with me for September so we can go over everything. Until then the rules don't change: chest pain at rest or lasting more than 15 minutes is a 911 call.

documents.title: F/u after cardiology consult
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen by cardiology 7/26: stable angina, positive exercise test, medical management, yearly f/u.

S: Chest pressure still comes with stairs or a hill, same as spring, stops within a few minutes of resting. No rest pain, no nighttime episodes, no syncope. He paces himself on the hill and takes the elevator at work most days. Diabetes plan unchanged, walking on level ground. Feet numb, no sores. Using sildenafil rarely; knows no nitrates with it.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, amlodipine 5, atorvastatin 20, aspirin 81, sildenafil 50 prn.

O: BP 132/79, HR 75, SpO2 96%, wt 85.8 kg (BMI 27.1).
No distress. Heart regular, normal S1/S2. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet: intact skin, calluses, reduced monofilament, diminished pulses - unchanged.

A/P:
1. Stable angina - per cardiology, medical management. Continue aspirin, atorvastatin, amlodipine. Reviewed warning signs again.
2. T2DM with CKD 1 and neuropathy - annual labs today.
3. HTN - amlodipine 5.
4. PAD - stable.
5. HM - flu and updated COVID vaccine today. Colonoscopy due 2029.

RTC 4-6 months.
